topics.name: Relative pronouns who / which / that / whose
Gerund vs infinitive (love to live, enjoy singing)

options: The bird sings a merry song.
The bird sing a merry song.
The bird singing a merry song.
questions.rule: A singular subject (the bird) takes a verb with -s in the simple present: sings.

options: The boy which loves the forest is my cousin.
The boy whose loves the forest is my cousin.
The boy who loves the forest is my cousin.
questions.rule: Use who for people. Which is for things and animals.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: loving
lover
loves

questions.rule: Aryan is singular, so the simple present verb takes -s: loves.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: sat
sit
sitting

questions.rule: An invitation uses the base verb: come ... and sit. Both verbs must match.

options: to sing
sings
sang
questions.rule: After love we can use the infinitive: love to sing.

options: isn't
doesn't
wasn't
questions.rule: A positive sentence with is takes the negative tag isn't it?
An invitation begins with the base verb: Come and sit.

chat: Would you like to come to the forest picnic on Sunday?
options: Yes, I would love come.
Yes, I would love to come.
Yes, I would loves to come.
questions.rule: Accept with I would love to + base verb. After would use love, not loves.

chat: You have packed your sweater, haven't you?
options: Yes, I have packing it.
Yes, I have packed it.
Yes, I has packed it.
questions.rule: Answer a tag question with the same tense: I have packed it.

questions.source: The shepherd lives in the forest.
options: Does the shepherd lives in the forest?
Does the shepherd live in the forest?
Do the shepherd live in the forest?
questions.rule: Use Does with a singular subject, and the base verb after it: Does ... live.

options: She enjoys walking in the sun.
She enjoys to walk in the sun.
She enjoy walking in the sun.
questions.rule: Enjoy is followed by a gerund (-ing): enjoys walking.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: You like birds, doesn't you?
You like birds, don't you?
You like birds, aren't you?
questions.rule: You like is simple present with you, so the tag is don't you?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: whose
which
who

questions.rule: The relative pronoun is the subject of loves, so use who, not whom.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: walked
walks
walking

questions.rule: After a preposition like of, use the gerund: fond of walking.

options: whose
who
whom
questions.rule: Whose shows possession: the tree's branches = the tree whose branches.

questions.after: up ambition is happy with simple things.
options: give
giving
gives
questions.rule: Who refers to He, which is singular, so use gives.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a question tag.
questions.rule: Positive statement with is + negative tag isn't it?

chat: What do you do on holidays?
options: I enjoy to read under a tree.
I enjoying read under a tree.
I enjoy reading under a tree.
questions.rule: Enjoy takes a gerund: I enjoy reading.

questions.source: I met a farmer. He grows fruit and nuts.
options: I met a farmer who grow fruit and nuts.
I met a farmer who grows fruit and nuts.
I met a farmer which grows fruit and nuts.
questions.rule: Who replaces He. A farmer is singular, so keep grows.

options: The birds are singing, aren't they?
The birds are singing, isn't it?
The birds are singing, don't they?
questions.rule: Use the same helper verb (are) in the negative and the pronoun they: aren't they?

options: The song that the bird sing is sweet.
The song who the bird sings is sweet.
The song that the bird sings is sweet.
questions.rule: Use that for things. Inside the clause, the bird is singular: sings.

options: Each of the birds have a sweet note.
Each of the bird has a sweet note.
Each of the birds has a sweet note.
questions.rule: Each of + plural noun takes a singular verb: Each of the birds has.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: hasn't
doesn't
won't

questions.rule: Brings is simple present with no helper, so the tag uses doesn't: doesn't it?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: sat
sits
sit

questions.rule: Want takes the infinitive: to + base verb = to sit.

questions.after: you join us for a picnic, please?
options: Does
Will
Are
questions.rule: A polite invitation can begin Will you + base verb. Does and Are do not fit you join.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a relative clause.
questions.rule: Who loves the sun tells us which man. It comes right after The man.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a gerund.
questions.rule: Enjoys is followed by a gerund: feeding.

chat: Who is that girl near the gate?
options: She is the girl which won the race.
She is the girl who win the race.
She is the girl who won the race.
questions.rule: Use who for a person, and the past won for a finished race.

questions.source: This is the bird. Its song is very sweet.
options: This is the bird who song is very sweet.
This is the bird whose song is very sweet.
This is the bird whose song are very sweet.
questions.rule: Whose replaces Its. Song is singular, so keep is.

options: The forest does not have many enemies.
The forest do not have many enemies.
The forest does not has many enemies.
questions.rule: Singular subject: does not + base verb have.

options: I have always loved watching the sunset.
I have always loved to watching the sunset.
I has always loved watching the sunset.
questions.rule: I have + past participle; love can take a gerund: loved watching.

options: Shall we go for a walk in the woods?
Shall we going for a walk in the woods?
Shall we goes for a walk in the woods?
questions.rule: Shall we + base verb makes a friendly suggestion: Shall we go.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: is
were
been

questions.rule: The subject is Both the hikers (plural) and the time is past, so use were.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: living
live
alive

questions.rule: Two people joined by and make a plural subject: Mr and Mrs Joshi live.

questions.before: You visited the bird sanctuary last week,
options: weren't
didn't
haven't
questions.rule: Visited is simple past with no helper, so the tag is didn't you?

options: will
don't
shall
questions.rule: A suggestion with Let's always takes the tag shall we?
Would you like to + base verb is a polite way to invite someone.

chat: You haven't seen a woodpecker, have you?
options: No, I haven't. I would love to seeing one.
No, I didn't seen. I would love to see one.
No, I haven't. I would love to see one.
questions.rule: Reply with the same helper: No, I haven't. After love to use the base verb.

chat: Does your school have a garden?
options: Yes, it does. It has a big neem tree too.
Yes, it do. It has a big neem tree too.
Yes, it does. It have a big neem tree too.
questions.rule: It is singular: it does and it has.

questions.source: Rohit has seen a deer in the forest.
options: Has Rohit saw a deer in the forest?
Has Rohit seen a deer in the forest?
Does Rohit has seen a deer in the forest?
questions.rule: Move the helper Has to the front and keep the past participle seen.

options: Anyone who loves nature and is happy with simple food is welcome here.
Anyone who love nature and is happy with simple food is welcome here.
Anyone who loves nature and are happy with simple food is welcome here.
questions.rule: Who refers to Anyone, which is singular: loves ... and is.

options: Instead of chase fame, he chose to live a quiet life in the woods.
Instead of chasing fame, he chose to lived a quiet life in the woods.
Instead of chasing fame, he chose to live a quiet life in the woods.
questions.rule: After the preposition of use a gerund (chasing); after chose to use the base verb (live).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: fill
filling
full

questions.rule: The subject is Many sweet songs (plural), not bird. So use fill.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: enjoy
enjoying
enjoyment

questions.rule: Who refers to my two cousins (plural), so the verb is enjoy.

questions.before: After a long day in the fields, the farmer looked forward to
options: rest
rests
resting
questions.rule: In look forward to, to is a preposition, so it takes a gerund: resting.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a question tag.
questions.rule: Nobody is negative, so the tag is positive, and it uses they: do they?

chat: Would you mind helping me plant these saplings?
options: Not at all. I would be happy to helping.
Not at all. I would be happy to help.
Not at all. I would being happy to help.
questions.rule: Not at all agrees to a Would you mind request. Use would be and happy to help.

chat: Why did you stop coming to practice?
options: I stopped to coming because I had hurt my ankle.
I stopped coming because I had hurted my ankle.
I stopped coming because I had hurt my ankle.
questions.rule: Stop + gerund means to give up doing something: stopped coming. Hurt stays hurt in the past.

questions.source: We rested under a banyan tree. It was more than a hundred years old.
options: We rested under a banyan tree who was more than a hundred years old.
We rested under a banyan tree which it was more than a hundred years old.
We rested under a banyan tree which was more than a hundred years old.
questions.rule: Which replaces It, so do not repeat it. Use which for things.

questions.source: There is an old banyan tree near the lake.
options: There is an old banyan tree near the lake, isn't it?
There is an old banyan tree near the lake, isn't there?
There is an old banyan tree near the lake, doesn't there?
questions.rule: When a sentence begins with There is, the tag repeats there, not it: isn't there?
